name: Elder
summary: Turn the phone into a handful of large, obvious things: calls, messages, camera, photos, WhatsApp. Everything else gets out of the way.
note: This is the one profile that works by keeping a short list rather than removing a long one, because the problem it solves is not bloat. It is choice. An elderly user staring at nine screens of icons is the thing we are fixing.

standard.label: Standard
standard.blurb: Keep the essentials plus anything already on the home screen. Bigger text, longer screen timeout, no screensaver.

extreme.label: Extreme
extreme.blurb: Keep only the essential roles: phone, messages, contacts, camera, gallery, clock, calculator, settings, WhatsApp, YouTube. Everything else with an icon is turned off.

ultra.label: Ultra
ultra.blurb: Phone, messages, contacts and camera. Nothing else. For someone who genuinely only wants a telephone.
ultra.warn: This removes WhatsApp, YouTube and the Play Store from view. Make sure that is what the person wants, not what you find tidy.

ops.label: Text size: large
ops.note: Equivalent to the second-largest step in Settings. Some older apps clip their own buttons past this.

ops.label: Screen stays on for 5 minutes
ops.note: A 30-second timeout is the single most common complaint from older users.

ops.label: Longer press before a long-press registers
ops.note: Stops accidental drag-and-drop and context menus for an unsteady hand.

ops.label: Touch feedback on
ops.note: Confirms a tap landed, which matters when you cannot feel the button.

suggest_note: A launcher with large tiles does more for an elderly user than any amount of debloating. Offered, never forced: switching someone's home screen without asking is its own kind of rude.
